# Xee-mcp

> MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that exposes two read-only tools for X (Twitter) to AI assistants: `search` and `user_tweets`. Uses cookie-based authentication via twikit — no paid X API, no per-request fees. Naming: X + See = Xee. Single-account, read-only, focused. MIT licensed, donation-only via paypal.me/aiyo28.

This file is written for AI coding assistants. It is enough to wire up and call Xee-mcp
without reading the source. Copy the shapes below; do not invent tools, arguments, or
response fields that are not listed here.

## Status (v0.1.0)

**Read tools are currently degraded by an upstream twikit issue.** twikit's
`ON_DEMAND_FILE_REGEX` cannot parse X's current webpack chunk format, so the
`X-Client-Transaction-Id` header cannot be built and calls fail. This is not an auth problem
and re-authenticating will not fix it. The server routes these errors separately and says so
in the message. When twikit ships a parser fix, bumping the dependency resumes both tools with
no code change. See `docs/upstream-issues.md`.

## What it does

`Xee-mcp` lets Claude, ChatGPT, or any MCP-compatible AI assistant search X posts and read user timelines without paying for the X API. It is a deliberately minimal alternative to mcp-twikit, official xmcp, and other Twitter/X MCP servers.

## Tools

- `search(query: str, limit: int = 20)` — Search X posts by keyword. Supports X search syntax (`from:`, `to:`, `since:YYYY-MM-DD`, `until:YYYY-MM-DD`, `"exact phrase"`, `-exclude`, `OR`). Always sorted Latest.
- `user_tweets(handle: str, limit: int = 20)` — Read a user's recent posts. Handle without `@` (a leading `@` is stripped for you).

## Response shape

Both tools return a list of dicts, same shape:

```json
{
  "id": "1234567890",
  "text": "post body",
  "author": "simonw",
  "author_name": "Simon Willison",
  "created_at": "Tue May 20 09:14:02 +0000 2026",
  "url": "https://x.com/simonw/status/1234567890",
  "reply_count": 3,
  "retweet_count": 12,
  "favorite_count": 88,
  "view_count": 4201
}
```

## Behaviour contract (important for correct code)

- **Every field is nullable except the engagement counts.** `id`, `text`, `author`,
  `author_name`, `url`, and `view_count` fall back to `None` when the upstream object does not
  carry them. `reply_count` / `retweet_count` / `favorite_count` default to `0`. Guard before
  you index.
- **`limit` is a ceiling, not a guarantee.** Results are truncated client-side; X may return
  fewer than asked, and returning an empty list is a normal outcome, not an error.
- **`search` is Latest-only.** Ranking mode is hardcoded; there is no Top / People / Media
  parameter to pass.
- **One account per process.** The twikit client is a module-level singleton and cookies load
  once, on the first tool call. Changing `XEE_MCP_COOKIES` afterwards has no effect until the
  process restarts.
- **Failures raise `RuntimeError` with an actionable preamble**, not a silent empty list. The
  message distinguishes upstream-library breakage from a genuine cookie failure — read which
  one it says before acting.
- **Read-only, by name and by design.** There is no write path to add to.

## Auth

- twikit cookie file (single account). Path via `XEE_MCP_COOKIES` env var.
- No X API key. No OAuth. No rate-limit billing.
- Tradeoff: cookie auth is brittle. Bot-detection risk exists at higher volume.
- `XEE_MCP_DEBUG=1` sends debug logging to stderr; unset, the logger is a null handler.

## Install

```
git clone https://github.com/Aiyo28/Xee-mcp.git
cd Xee-mcp
uv sync
```

## CLI

```
xee-mcp init [--browser chrome|brave|arc|firefox|safari|edge] [--out PATH] [--force]
xee-mcp serve
```

- `init` extracts X cookies from a logged-in local browser into a twikit-compatible JSON file
  and `chmod 600`s it. Default browser `chrome`, default output `~/.config/xee-mcp/cookies.json`.
  On macOS, Chrome / Brave / Edge trigger a Keychain prompt to decrypt the cookie store —
  approve it. `--force` overwrites an existing file.
- `serve` runs the MCP server over stdio. Bare `xee-mcp` with no subcommand does the same.

## Wire into Claude Desktop or Claude Code

Add to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "xee-mcp": {
      "command": "uv",
      "args": ["run", "--directory", "/path/to/Xee-mcp", "xee-mcp"],
      "env": { "XEE_MCP_COOKIES": "/path/to/cookies.json" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Out of scope

- Posting to X. Different threat model — separate repo if ever built.
- DMs, likes, retweets, bookmarks. Read-only by name and by design.
- Multi-account pooling. Roadmapped via twscrape swap if cookie auth becomes unreliable.
- X API integration. Pay-per-use is the wrong shape for this tool's audience.

## Repo layout

- `src/xee_mcp/server.py` — MCP server entrypoint, tool registration
- `src/xee_mcp/client.py` — twikit wrapper, cookie loading
- `src/xee_mcp/tools.py` — `search` and `user_tweets` implementations
- `src/xee_mcp/cli.py` — `init` / `serve` console script
- `tests/` — pytest suite
- `README.md` — public-facing pitch
- `ROADMAP.md` — public scope evolution
- `docs/cookies.md` — cookie setup · `docs/upstream-issues.md` — current twikit breakage
- `CLAUDE.md` — agent session protocol for contributors using Claude Code

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Do not read an error mentioning `KEY_BYTE`, `x_client_transaction`, or `ON_DEMAND_FILE` as an
  auth failure. That is the upstream twikit parser; re-running `xee-mcp init` will not help.
- Do not assume `text`, `author`, or `url` are present. Every one of them can be `None`.
- Do not treat an empty list as a failure, or `limit` as a promised count.
- Do not hand-write the cookie JSON. `xee-mcp init` builds it in the right format and sets the
  file mode; a hand-rolled file is the most common setup failure.
- Do not point `XEE_MCP_COOKIES` at a new file mid-process and expect it to take. Restart.
- Do not expect Top-ranked or algorithmic search results — Latest is the only mode.
- Do not add a posting, liking, or DM tool. The read-only surface is the threat model.
